title: Review: Graphs and data analysis; Estimation and orders of magnitude; Nuclear structure and notation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; N01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS03-1#N.15, MS04-1#N.3, N01-1#N.10, MS04-1#N.6, N01-1#N.3, MS04-1#N.10, N01-1#N.7a, N01-1#N.5. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Order of magnitude
items.clue: The nearest power of ten to a value.

items.label: y-intercept
items.clue: Value on the vertical axis where x = 0.

items.label: Nucleon number
items.clue: Symbol A: the total count of protons plus neutrons, 56 for iron-56.

items.label: Proton number
items.clue: Symbol Z: it fixes which element an atom is, 26 for every iron atom.

questions.stem: A best-fit line has gradient 2.50. The steepest line through all the error bars has gradient 2.65 (same units). What is the percentage uncertainty in the gradient?
Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: A nucleus of potassium-40 is written in nuclear notation as ⁴⁰₁₉K. Which statement about this nucleus is correct?
A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: Predict first. Nucleons in a nucleus are about 10⁻¹⁵ m apart, while the nuclei of neighbouring atoms in a solid are about 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Why does the strong nuclear force bind the nucleons within each nucleus but have no effect between neighbouring nuclei?

options.text: Its range is so short that it is negligible at separations much above 10⁻¹⁵ m.
It is a repulsive force between nuclei, as every nucleus carries positive charge.
The electrons around each nucleus block the force from reaching other nuclei.
It falls as 1/r², so at 10⁻¹⁰ m it is 10¹⁰ times weaker than it is inside a nucleus.

questions.stem: Predict first. Carbon-12 (¹²₆C) and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) are isotopes of carbon. Which statement about these two nuclides is correct?

options.text: They contain the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Both contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
Their atoms have different chemical properties, as their nuclei differ.
Their nuclei are identical, but their atoms have different numbers of electrons.
